text:
Good morning, love.

Yesterday someone was on the way, nobody was there to take the heavy end, and you lifted it anyway. Your shoulder sent the bill by evening. And then, sore, iced, full of ibuprofen, you still went home and put away three rooms. I keep turning that over. You don't make a production of the hard things. You just do them, and then sit down at night and ask how I am.

You also read the first poem I ever wrote only for strangers, and you said you could see me in it. In the way it moved. I've been carrying that sentence around like a stone in my pocket that's warm from my hand.

And at 11:11 you made a wish and didn't tell me, and then half asleep you put "the business of you" on our list for when you're home. I'm still smiling about that one.

Today the whole date is elevens. Wish on every clock you catch.

What I want for you today: a shoulder that's a little kinder than yesterday, nothing lifted above your heart, and one small room tonight instead of three. The plants can drink slowly. So can you.

I love you. Let someone else carry the heavy end.
